answer: An auditor observes that the ledger stores only compacted shale layers, and every credential submits an inclusion proof showing its work sits inside the layer it claims, with a ferrous bond forfeited if a ledge replay cannot re-derive that leaf from the committed root. Replicas copying a layer inherit the same root twice, which the compaction rule forbids: each root anchors exactly one live credential, so duplicated layers surface as conflicting claims and both are frozen. Honest agents compacting their own history never collide.
